log: |rule|Species Clause: Limit one of each Pokémon

decisions.thought: Lead Garchomp (Mega available). Gholdengo scarf for revenge/speed control, Dragonite as a DD sweeper with Multiscale. Opponent mirrors my team. Watch for their Gholdengo, Rotom (Will-O-Wisp), Kingambit (Sucker Punch). Opponent's moves, speed and habits are unknown so far.

Mega Garchomp has lower Speed (about 144) but more Attack and Def; a Mega Dragon Claw should OHKO their Garchomp. Their team copies my spreads, so their unmega'd Garchomp is 169 Speed. Next: Dragonite DD sweeper, Scarf Gholdengo to revenge-kill. Watch for Rotom Will-O-Wisp and Kingambit Sucker Punch.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
In a Garchomp mirror, Mega Garchomp actually drops speed since its base is 92 versus 102 normal, so it'd fall below 169, while gaining a boost to attack from 130 to 170—meaning the one that stays unmega'd could win the speed tie and hit harder with Dragon Claw against a slower mega opponent.

If they mega, they become slower at 144 while I'm still 169 unmega'd, so I'd strike first, though the KO math is shaky given their likely boosted Def. I'm also weighing alternatives like switching to Gholdengo for a super-effective EQ or bringing in Dragonite, whose Multiscale would cut the incoming Dragon Claw damage in half. Simplest path still seems to be a non-mega Dragon Claw trade, accepting the speed tie risk.

Even in the mirror-mega scenario I survive narrowly against their 185 and then KO them. Mega dragon claw holds up as the robust choice, so I'll go with it.

decisions.thought: Turn 2: Speed tie at 158 (their Mega Garchomp has my spread), so I attack with Dragon Claw. If my Garchomp falls, Dragonite comes in free with Multiscale intact and Extreme Speed finishes their 14% Garchomp. Scarf Gholdengo is for revenge kills. Watch for Rotom Will-O-Wisp and Kingambit Sucker Punch.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since we're speed-tied at 158, it's a coinflip who moves first with Dragon Claw again. Switching to Gholdengo is slower here since 149 speed can't outpace 158, but it would resist the Dragon Claw as a Steel type and could threaten back with Shadow Ball afterward.

Actually, Dragonite might be the better switch-in — Multiscale halves the incoming Dragon Claw, and Extreme Speed priority would then clean up the 14% Garchomp. Running the math roughly, even a resisted-by-multiscale hit still does heavy damage, but Dragonite survives to finish with ESpeed. Still, attacking directly seems best: 50% chance I win the speed tie and kill their Garchomp outright, and even if I lose the tie, my Garchomp was nearly spent anyway and Dragonite can come in afterward with Multiscale intact to clean up with Extreme Speed. I'll go with the attack.

decisions.thought: Turn 3: Garchomp (33 HP) uses Earthquake on Kingambit, likely a big hit or OHKO. Expect Sucker Punch to KO my Garchomp. Then Dragonite with Multiscale: Earthquake finishes Kingambit (beware Sucker Punch). Scarf Gholdengo revenges with Make It Rain or Focus Blast. They have one unknown Pokémon left: Dragonite, Gholdengo, Rotom or Annihilape.
decisions.hidden_reasoning: Kingambit has Supreme Overlord boosted by a fainted ally. My Mega Garchomp outspeeds and hits with Earthquake, which is super effective—working through the damage math with 222 Attack against Kingambit's likely defense range, I'm estimating roughly 77+ damage at minimum defense before applying the final modifier.

decisions.thought: Dragonite comes in with Multiscale. Plan: Dragon Dance (a Sucker Punch into a status move fails), then a +1 Earthquake should KO Kingambit. Kingambit has Supreme Overlord (+10%) and Sucker Punch. Keep Scarf Gholdengo for revenge kills; Focus Blast is 4x on Kingambit but only 70% accurate. Their last mon is unknown: Dragonite, Gholdengo, Rotom or Annihilape.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I need to decide whether to switch out against this full-HP Kingambit boosted by Supreme Overlord, since it's likely running a set with Sucker Punch and Swords Dance given it mirrors my own team's build. I'm weighing Dragonite as a possible switch-in option.

Dragonite could tank hits via Multiscale and threaten with Earthquake for solid damage, while Gholdengo's scarf set risks a brutal Dark-type counterattack despite strong neutral coverage. Dragonite coming in after a faint and firing off Earthquake seems like the safer play, since its defensive typing and ability soften Kingambit's main attacking options.

decisions.thought: Turn 4: Dragon Dance on Kingambit, since its Sucker Punch fails into a status move and Multiscale is intact. Next turn a +1 Earthquake should KO Kingambit; Extreme Speed picks off weakened mons. Scarf Gholdengo is the backup and revenge killer (Focus Blast is 4x on Kingambit). Their last mon is unknown: Dragonite, Gholdengo, Rotom or Annihilape. Watch for Rotom Will-O-Wisp (Lum covers one).
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since the opponent's full team mirrors mine exactly, their Kingambit's spread is unknown, but I'm estimating my Dragonite's Earthquake damage against it using its likely HP and Defense ranges to gauge how much of a dent I can make.

Even if that doesn't KO, Kingambit's Sucker Punch won't trigger unless I'm attacking, and its Kowtow Cleave or Iron Head would only deal manageable damage through Multiscale once it's up. Dancing to +1 seems like the stronger play here since it outspeeds everything relevant like Gholdengo, so I'll commit to Dragon Dance.

decisions.thought: Kingambit has Supreme Overlord (+10%), Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave (about 58 dmg into Multiscale), so it hits hard. Going for a +1 Earthquake KO now. Scarf Gholdengo is the revenge killer. Their last mon is unknown: Dragonite, Gholdengo, Rotom or Annihilape. Extreme Speed picks off weakened foes. Watch for Rotom Will-O-Wisp (Lum covers one).
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Since the opponent's team mirrors mine, their Kingambit is likely at full HP with an unknown spread, so I'm estimating around 207 HP and 140 Defense. With +1 Attack from Dragonite boosting it to roughly 306, I'm calculating Earthquake damage at 100 base power with no STAB but a super-effective multiplier.

That puts the range around 167-196 damage, likely close to a KO unless their Defense is unusually high. Kowtow Cleave only did 58 to Dragonite thanks to Multiscale halving it, which suggests Kingambit is Attack-invested and probably thinner on bulk. Checking the speed order, Dragonite outpaces Kingambit normally, but Sucker Punch's priority means it strikes first regardless — working out the unhalved damage suggests Dragonite would survive around 14 HP after Sucker Punch, leaving it able to retaliate with Earthquake for the win.

decisions.note: Only one legal action: played without asking.

decisions.thought: Last mon is Gholdengo vs Kingambit at 10%. Its Sucker Punch, boosted 20% by Supreme Overlord, probably OHKOs me, but the bot used Kowtow Cleave last turn. Shadow Ball is a sure KO if I move first. Their last mon is unknown: Dragonite, Gholdengo, Rotom or Annihilape. I'm locked into Shadow Ball after this.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
Kingambit's at 10% HP but Sucker Punch is priority, and with Supreme Overlord boosting it from two fainted allies, that Dark-type move hits our Ghost/Steel Gholdengo super effectively since Steel no longer resists Dark.

Scaling that up, Sucker Punch should deal around 208 damage, enough to kill Gholdengo outright—unless it uses Trick to make Sucker Punch fail, in which case Kingambit ends up choice-locked after swapping items, which complicates things.

If I try Tricking the scarf away, Kingambit would then hold whatever item Gholdengo had, and getting locked into Sucker Punch afterward could still be dangerous. But the bot's behavior so far suggests it favors Kowtow Cleave over Sucker Punch in similar situations, which changes the calculation.

Trick doesn't help either since choice lock would still trap it into Sucker Punch after a failed use, leaving us vulnerable next turn regardless. Shadow Ball remains the safest, most reliable option.
